gloss: A very large sea mammal that breathes air through a hole on top of its head.
examples: We saw a *whale* breach about a hundred yards off the boat.
*Whales* migrate down this coast every winter.
The museum has a life-size blue *whale* hanging from the ceiling.

gloss: A smart, playful sea mammal with a long snout.
examples: A pair of *dolphins* followed the ferry for almost a mile.
My daughter wants to swim with *dolphins* on our trip.
A *dolphin* is a mammal, not a fish.

gloss: A small sea mammal like a dolphin but shorter, with a blunt nose.
examples: *Porpoises* are stockier than dolphins and have blunter faces.
We spotted a *porpoise* in the bay at dawn.
The crew pulled in the nets to avoid catching a *porpoise*.
contrast: The ending is said like the word *purpose*, not 'poyz'.

gloss: A sea mammal with short flippers that comes ashore to rest.
examples: A *seal* was sunning itself on the rocks below the trail.
The far end of the dock is crowded with *seals*.
We watched a baby *seal* learn to swim.

gloss: A large seal with visible ear flaps that can walk on its front flippers.
examples: The *sea lions* down at the pier are a tourist attraction.
A *sea lion* can move surprisingly fast on land.
You can hear the *sea lions* barking from three blocks away.

gloss: A huge Arctic sea mammal with two long tusks and thick whiskers.
examples: A full-grown *walrus* can weigh more than a ton.
The zoo's new exhibit has two *walruses*.
He grew a mustache that made him look like a *walrus*.

gloss: A small furry water animal with webbed feet and a long tail.
examples: A sea *otter* floated on its back cracking open a clam.
*Otters* hold hands so they don't drift apart while they sleep.
An *otter* slid down the muddy bank and disappeared.

gloss: A slow, heavy plant-eating sea mammal of warm shallow water.
examples: *Manatees* gather in the warm water near the power plant.
A *manatee* can eat a tenth of its body weight in a day.
We rented kayaks and paddled out to see the *manatees*.

gloss: A large black-and-white whale that hunts in family groups.
examples: An *orca* surfaced right next to the kayak.
*Orcas* hunt together and teach their young how to do it.
The park stopped keeping *orcas* years ago.

gloss: An Arctic whale whose long straight tusk sticks out from its head.
examples: A *narwhal*'s tusk is really one giant tooth.
*Narwhals* live under the Arctic ice year-round.
Sailors used to sell *narwhal* tusks as unicorn horns.
